column1: # Player-facing settings: the iOS launcher (dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift) and the Mac app's settings window (dm/mac/Launcher.swift) show them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.

# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json; build_ipa.sh, and dm/mac/pack_app.py through the NSP script): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host reads when the game starts; one an env file sets
# (Documents/env.txt, the bundle's dm/env.txt) is shown but kept. Diagnostic switches stay environment-only, so they are not listed here. The player's page is docs/settings.md.
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets

#   kind      choice: values value=label,..., an option only some games have with ?<shown>&<shown> after its label (languages: the game's own, from its control data; every language when it has none, with a note); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage;
#             toggle: values - (on sets 1, off 0) or <on>/<off>, the two values the variable takes (on/off)
#   default   a value (a toggle's: 1 on, 0 off); DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the IPA build's setting (build_ipa.sh)
#             <ios>|<mac> selects the platform's default before resolving a profile macro or build variable
#   shown     Conditions may be joined with &. runtime:DM_VARIABLE=value requires a complete runtime manifest matching the rewritten module (Mac only).

#             always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key (a stub in the game's build, patch_nso.py); languages>1 (more than one to pick, so also when the control data lists none); gfxapi:<API>: the packer's GFXAPI;
#             platform:<ios | mac>: the app's platform (SETTINGS_PLATFORM, ios when unset), for a switch only that platform's front end reads
#   section   Game, Controls or Performance: a heading on the single settings screen. Rows appear in table order within each section
#             Reset to tested defaults clears all launcher choices; values fixed by an env file stay
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (may be empty; only for a setting with a cost: latency, memory, heat)
#   meta      optional, key=value pairs separated by ; (settings.py META lists the keys; docs/frontends.md, The settings list, describes them):
#             level=basic  a setting a front end shows first;  needs=<VAR>=<value>  a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value

column8: Full-output modes are experimental. Start with 1080p; check scanning and cutscenes. 1800p retains the confirmed rendering path.
Lets the native controller lower scene resolution under load. Off holds the selected maximum. MP4 reference modes keep their original behavior.
Sharper ground and walls seen at an angle. 16x costs little on a Mac.
Sharper shadow edges. High uses 24 MB more GPU memory; Ultra 120 MB and more GPU time.
Keeps objects detailed further away. Far and Very far move the switch to simpler models 2 or 4 times further out; Maximum always draws the most detailed model. More GPU time.
Fog and light shafts at full resolution: cleaner edges around objects. Uses more GPU time and 100 MB or more GPU memory at 1800p.
Uses more GPU time and can increase heat.
Fill crops the game's 16:9 picture to cover the screen. Health bars, subtitles or maps near the edges can be cut off. A full-screen picture without cropping needs a patch for each game.
Plays Joy-Con 2 and Pro Controller 2 over Bluetooth: hold Sync on one during the game to pair it. macOS asks once for Bluetooth access.
Renders about a quarter more pixels: a little slower and warmer.
Softens loud moments instead of clipping them: fewer crackles in loud fights.
Up to one frame more display latency.
Keeps a pipeline archive; uses more memory.
The first start waits a few minutes for it, once.
